actions.justification: Mandatory first step — patient is critically ill with hypotension (BP 78/45), tachycardia (HR 130), severe hypoxia (SpO2 82%), and tachypnea (RR 30). Formal vital signs assessment is required to establish baseline and guide urgency of interventions.

Mandatory — Wells score stratification is required per ESC PE guidelines to confirm clinical probability of PE and guide diagnostic and therapeutic pathway, especially given the need to consider thrombolysis in this hemodynamically unstable patient.

Mandatory — D-dimer is part of the initial PE workup per ESC guidelines. Although in high-probability/massive PE D-dimer may not be the deciding factor, it is a required assessment step and part of the diagnostic confirmation pathway.
Patient has critical hypoxia with SpO2 82% — immediate supplemental oxygen is required to prevent cardiac arrest and improve oxygenation in massive PE.
ECG is a key initial diagnostic step in PE workup to assess for right heart strain pattern (S1Q3T3, RBBB, sinus tachycardia) and rule out other causes of hemodynamic compromise.
Patient is in obstructive shock (BP 78/45, MAP 56) — cautious IV fluid resuscitation to maintain RV preload while further assessment and definitive therapy are arranged.

CT pulmonary angiography is the gold-standard for confirming PE diagnosis. Patient has high clinical probability (shock, hypoxia, tachycardia) and requires confirmatory imaging before thrombolysis, if clinically stable enough to transport.

Bedside echocardiogram can rapidly confirm right heart strain/RV dysfunction consistent with massive PE, and may serve as confirmatory test if patient is too unstable for CT-PA. Can also assess for other causes of shock.

Patient has refractory hypotension (MAP 56, BP 78/45) despite IV fluids. Vasopressor support (norepinephrine) is indicated to maintain perfusion pressure while diagnostic workup proceeds and definitive treatment (thrombolysis) is prepared.

ECG (via imaging action) to assess for signs of right heart strain (S1Q3T3, right bundle branch block) in this massive PE presentation. Note: order_ecg is already done, but order_imaging_ecg is a distinct available action.

Bedside echocardiogram to rapidly assess right ventricular strain/dilation and confirm massive PE in this hemodynamically unstable patient (HR 130, BP 78/45, SpO2 82%), which will guide thrombolysis decision.
Chest X-ray to evaluate for alternative causes of hypoxia and dyspnea and assess baseline cardiopulmonary status in this critically ill patient with suspected massive PE.
ABG needed to assess severity of hypoxemia (SpO2 82%), acid-base status, and degree of respiratory failure in this massive PE patient
BNP will quantify right ventricular strain and help risk-stratify this massive PE with hemodynamic collapse

Active lower GI bleed is a relative contraindication to systemic thrombolysis; catheter-directed thrombectomy or catheter-directed thrombolysis may be the preferred reperfusion strategy — IR consult is urgent

Patient has massive PE with shock (BP 78/45, HR 130, SpO2 82%, MAP 56). ESC guidelines strongly recommend thrombolysis for massive PE with hemodynamic instability. Although active GI bleed is a relative contraindication, the life-threatening nature of massive PE makes thrombolysis the indicated treatment. Interventional radiology has already been consulted.
CBC is urgently needed to assess hemoglobin/hematocrit in context of active GI bleed, platelet count before thrombolysis, and overall hematologic status.
Coagulation studies (PT/INR, PTT) are essential prior to and during thrombolysis to guide dosing and monitor bleeding risk in this patient with active GI bleed.
